He celebrated with confidence, knowing that his team needed him against a Spanish side filled with incredible talent. Spain had players like Sergio Ramos, Gerard Pique, Sergio Busquets, Andres Iniesta and David Silva, but Ronaldo was determined to make the difference. Spain did not panic after conceding. They continued passing the ball, controlling possession and searching for an equaliser. Their patience eventually paid off when Diego Costa received the ball, battled against Portuguese defenders and found the net in the 24th minute. The match was level at 1-1, and Spain started to look dangerous. Portugal had to defend carefully because Spain could punish even the smallest mistake. However, Ronaldo was still waiting for another opportunity. Just before half-time, Ronaldo received the ball outside the penalty area and fired a powerful shot towards goal. David de Gea got his hands to it, but the ball slipped through his grasp and rolled into the net. Portugal were leading 2-1, and Ronaldo had scored twice before the break. It was a massive moment because Spain had been fighting their way back into the game, only for Ronaldo to put Portugal ahead again. His celebration showed how much the goal meant to him, while Spanish supporters were left shocked by the mistake. After half-time, Spain returned with even more determination. They knew they could not afford to let Portugal control the match, and they began pushing forward in search of another goal. In the 55th minute, Diego Costa scored his second of the night after Spain worked the ball into a dangerous position. Portugal's defenders struggled to stop him, and suddenly the score was 2-2. The game had become a battle between two teams that refused to give up, with every attack carrying the possibility of changing everything. Spain then completed their comeback in the 58th minute. Nacho Fernandez received the ball outside the penalty area and struck an incredible shot that flew into the net after hitting the inside of the post. It was a spectacular goal, and Spain had taken the lead for the first time. Portugal were now losing 3-2, despite Ronaldo having scored twice. Nacho's celebration reflected the importance of the moment, while Spain looked ready to take control of one of the biggest matches of the group stage. Portugal needed someone to rescue them, and their captain was not finished yet. Ronaldo continued fighting, searching for space and trying to create chances against a Spanish defence that was becoming increasingly confident. As the clock moved towards the final minutes, Portugal won a free kick in a dangerous position. It was the kind of moment that could define a World Cup campaign, and Ronaldo stepped forward with the responsibility resting on his shoulders. In the 88th minute, Ronaldo placed the ball down, took a few steps backwards and prepared to strike. He knew that Spain had one of the strongest goalkeepers in the world, but he still backed himself to score.
